body:
## What this changes

Today `_publish.py` posts `card.md` as one top-level issue comment. This changes it to post a **PR review** — `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pr}/reviews` with `event: "COMMENT"`, never `APPROVE` or `REQUEST_CHANGES` — with the findings that can be anchored attached to the lines they are about, and everything else left in the review body.

The mechanism is ported from ROCm/ATOM's `feat/atom-review-bot`. **ATOM's bot has never posted successfully** (its machine account is flagged), so this code has never run against live GitHub. aiter's bot *is* live, which is why this is a draft — see "What is not verified" below.

## Why

Across the **61 real cards this bot has already published on this repo**, there are 229 findings. 120 (52%) cite a `file:line`, and 65 of those lines are inside the PR's own diff. Those are findings a reader would rather meet next to the code than half-way down a wall of prose.

Measured on ten of those real cards, replayed against the diffs they were written for:

| PR | findings | anchored | left in summary | card chars (today) | summary chars (after) | change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #5742 | 2 | 1 | 1 | 1878 | 1340 | −538 |
| #5767 | 3 | 0 | 3 | 2701 | 2341 | −360 |
| #5776 | 3 | 0 | 3 | 3249 | 2866 | −383 |
| #6184 | 5 | 3 | 2 | 4928 | 2908 | −2020 |
| #6188 | 5 | 0 | 5 | 4108 | 3752 | −356 |
| #6343 | 3 | 0 | 3 | 3094 | 2804 | −290 |
| #6364 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1382 | 535 | −847 |
| #6442 | 5 | 2 | 3 | 3909 | 2632 | −1277 |
| #6756 | 4 | 3 | 1 | 3110 | 1635 | −1475 |
| #6815 | 5 | 1 | 4 | 4666 | 3360 | −1306 |
| **total** | **36** | **11** | **25** | **33025** | **24173** | **−8852 (27%)** |

Every card gets shorter. But read the rows honestly: where nothing anchors (#5767, #6188, #6343, #5776) the card only loses ~300–400 characters, and that is the bold one-sentence PR summary the review body omits — not the mechanism working. The real win is the four rows with ≥2 anchors. **On aiter, only 28% of findings anchor** (65/229), against the ~50% ATOM measured, because aiter findings more often cite a line of *context* code the PR did not touch, or carry no `file:line` at all. 35 of 61 cards would get at least one inline comment; 26 would be unchanged in substance.

## The index is not decoration

The review body ends with a one-line index of every finding that went inline:

```
**3 finding(s) posted inline, on the lines they are about:**
- `aiter/ops/shuffle.py:23` — imports `_FLYDSL_USE_HERD` without pinning it
```

Without it, a reader of the summary alone cannot tell whether three findings exist elsewhere or none do — and an invisible finding reads exactly like a finding that was never made.

## Anchoring is a privilege a finding earns

`check_citations.py` comes across from ATOM and is wired in as `run_one.sh` step 3c. It writes `citations.txt`, `_lib.py` collects it into the report dir, and `_publish.py` refuses to anchor **any** finding carrying a citation the checker flagged — even if another citation in the same sentence would resolve. A top-level card that cites a wrong line is a flaw the reader works around; an inline comment on a wrong line lands in the author's working view and is visibly wrong, and a reviewer who gets burned once stops reading the rest.

With no `citations.txt` at all, nothing anchors and the whole card stays in the summary — i.e. exactly what this bot posts today. That is the intended degradation.

The checker never gates the run (`|| true`, not in `_gates.py`). It ran 1-for-2 on real cards; a 50%-precision heuristic that *withholds correct reviews* costs more than the defect it catches. It did earn its keep here: on #5776 it flagged `aiter/mla.py:2693`, and that finding correctly lost its inline slot.

## Degrade-to-summary

A review is all-or-nothing: one `comments[]` entry naming a line GitHub will not accept fails the whole call, **summary included** — strictly worse than the issue comment this replaces. So a refusal retries the same endpoint with the anchors folded back into the body and says `[ANCHORS REFUSED -- folded into summary]`. A review that silently sheds half its findings reads exactly like a review that only had the other half. Two tests pin this.

## Adapted, not transcribed

Where aiter differs from ATOM and what changed as a result:

- **Card shape.** aiter's `SKILL.md` writes `Review (advisory):`, not ATOM's `Review:`, and adds a `Perf (advisory|deterministic):` line ATOM has no counterpart for. ATOM's literal `"Review:"` / `"Validation"` prefixes would have dropped **all three** status lines, leaving a summary with no verdict in it. The summary now matches on the bare word and keeps every one, in card order. Pinned by a test.
- **Dedup.** aiter's `BOT` is overridable via `AITER_BOT_NAME`; the dedup marker is deliberately **not** derived from it, or a box with that var set would repost over every review the real bot already published. And `already_posted()` now searches **both** the issues-comments and the reviews endpoints — aiter's markers are sitting in live issue comments right now, and a check that only read reviews would repost on top of all of them. Both pinned by tests.
- **Env names.** `AITER_BOT_TOKEN(_FILE)`, `AITER_BOT_REPO`, repo default `ROCm/aiter`, status file `.aiter-review-status`, annotation title `aiter-bot` — all kept as aiter had them. `_api_raw()` (the `.diff` media type) is new; aiter had no caller for it.
- **`check_citations.py` provenance.** Its measurements are ATOM's and have not been rerun on aiter's cards; the docstring now says so instead of presenting them as local facts. Its "ambiguous bare basename" comment was recounted against this tree (aiter has 8 `utils.py`, 7 `quant.py`).
- **`_lib.py`.** `citations.txt` joins `OPTIONAL`, not `REQUIRED`: a run whose worker died before writing a card has no citations to check, and absence is not a defect.
- **No divergence was flattened.** aiter's `_publish.py` was ATOM's minus the anchoring work, plus the env-overridable `REPO`/`BOT`; both overrides are kept.
- **Untouched:** `.github/scripts/pr_self_review.py` is a separate system that PATCHes its own comment in place. It is not this skill and nothing here goes near it. The workflow YAML is also untouched.

## Guards

`check_prompts.py` gains three checks:

- `check_publish_review_is_advisory` — the event stays `COMMENT`, `APPROVE`/`REQUEST_CHANGES` appear nowhere in the file, and there is **exactly one** POST call site, `pulls/{pr}/reviews`.
- `check_publish_needs_post_flag` — `_publish.py` falls back to `~/.git-credentials` on the self-hosted box, a human PAT with write access, so `GITHUB_TOKEN` scoping does not stop it posting at all; the missing `--post` flag is the only closure. If the workflow ever grants `issues: write` or `pull-requests: write`, the invocation must pass `--post` explicitly.
- `check_anchoring_has_a_citation_check` — `run_one.sh` → `citations.txt` → `_lib.py` → `_publish.py` cannot be half-removed in silence, because that degradation looks identical to a card whose findings simply cite nothing.

`selftest.sh` now runs `_publish_test.py` (17 cases: the `--post` closure, the anchoring rule, dedup, the degrade-to-summary fallback), and says **out loud** when `pytest` is absent rather than passing over it — a check that did not run is not a check that passed.

### Verification, verbatim, on a clean tree built with `git archive HEAD`

```
$ bash .claude/skills/review-pr/selftest.sh | tail -1
=== 84 green / 0 red ===

$ python3 .claude/skills/review-pr/check_prompts.py | tail -1
OK: 0 drift(s)

$ python3 -m pytest .claude/skills/review-pr/_publish_test.py -q
.................                                                        [100%]
17 passed in 0.15s
```

(Baseline on `origin/main` was `83 green / 0 red` and `OK: 0 drift(s)`; the extra green is the new pytest block.)

`preflight.sh` on the same tree: `20 green / 1 red`. The red is pre-existing and environmental — the self-hosted runner is not installed as a systemd service — and is untouched by this change.

## What is **not** verified ⚠️

This is why the PR is a draft.

- **Nothing was posted to any real PR.** Every run above was dry-run or stubbed. All PR data was fetched read-only.
- **No live GitHub review call has ever been made by this code**, here or in ATOM. The anchor rules (`side: "RIGHT"`, `line` must be in the diff, `commit_id` must be the head) are from the API docs and ATOM's reasoning, not from a response.
- **`AITER_BOT_TOKEN`'s scope — resolved.** Creating a PR review needs `Pull requests: write`, where posting an issue comment needs only `Issues: write`, so a fine-grained PAT carrying only the latter would have failed every review and lost the card — a regression the anchor fallback does not cover, since that fallback handles a bad *anchor*, not a token that cannot create reviews at all. The token holder has confirmed the scope is sufficient. Noted here rather than deleted because the next person to rotate that PAT needs to know the publish path depends on it.
- The ten-card replay used each PR's head as it stands now, and only PRs whose head still matches the SHA in the card's marker, so the diffs are the ones the findings were written against. The 61-card population figures used current diffs, so for PRs that have moved since review they are an approximation.
- `citations.txt` has never been produced by a real `run_one.sh` on this repo — the ten used here were generated by running the shipped `check_citations.py` against each PR's real head tree, which is what step 3c does, but not inside a real run.

## Suggested way to land this

Check the PAT scope, then run `_publish.py <pr> --payload` (dry-run, posts nothing) on one real PR and read the JSON, before marking ready.

## PR Self-Review

### Reviewed revision

`0d4a88bd74d6`

### Behavior and intent

`_publish.py` posted the review card as one top-level issue comment. On ten real
`aiter-bot` cards that comment averages 3300 characters of dense prose, and a single
finding averages ~900 — a paragraph each, in a wall nobody reads to the end. Half the
findings cite a `file:line`, so some of them can be attached to the code they are about
instead.

It now posts `POST /pulls/{n}/reviews` with `event: "COMMENT"` — never `APPROVE` or
`REQUEST_CHANGES`; this bot does not gate merges — anchoring the findings whose cited
line is inside the diff, and keeping the rest, plus a one-line index of the anchored
ones, in the review body. The index matters: without it a reader of the summary cannot
tell whether findings exist elsewhere or none do, and an invisible finding reads exactly
like one that was never made.

Anchoring is gated on `check_citations.py`, ported here from ATOM along with the
`run_one.sh` step and `_lib.OPTIONAL` entry that produce and collect `citations.txt`.
A finding whose citation the checker could not resolve is not anchored: an inline
comment on the wrong line lands in the author's working view and is visibly wrong, and
a reviewer burned once stops reading the rest.

### Validation and unverified scope

Validated, on a clean tree built with `git archive HEAD`:

```
bash .claude/skills/review-pr/selftest.sh | tail -1   → === 84 green / 0 red ===
python3 .claude/skills/review-pr/check_prompts.py     → OK: 0 drift(s)
python3 -m pytest .claude/skills/review-pr/_publish_test.py -q → 17 passed
```

Baseline on `origin/main` before the change: 83 green / 0 red, 0 drift. Measured on ten
real published cards replayed against the diffs they were written for: 36 findings, 11
anchored, summary 33025 → 24173 characters (−27%). The win is concentrated in the four
cards with ≥2 anchors; cards where nothing anchors barely shrink, and the PR body says so.

**Unverified: no live GitHub review call has ever been made by this code, here or in
ATOM.** The anchor rules — `side: "RIGHT"`, the line having to be inside a hunk,
`commit_id` = head — come from the API documentation and reasoning, not from a response.
The degrade-to-summary fallback has been exercised only against a stub that refuses any
payload carrying `comments[]`. Also unverified: `citations.txt` has never been produced
by a real `run_one.sh` on this repo, and the 61-card population figures (52% cited, 28%
anchorable) used each PR's current diff, which for PRs that moved after review is an
approximation. The ten-card table is exact.

`AITER_BOT_TOKEN`'s scope was the one risk that could have made this a regression —
creating a review needs `Pull requests: write` where an issue comment needs only
`Issues: write`, and a token lacking it would fail every review and lose the card. The
token holder has confirmed the scope is sufficient.

### PR-specific question

**The boundary this introduces: a review is all-or-nothing.** GitHub rejects the entire
call — summary included — if any single `comments[]` entry names a line it will not
accept. Today's single comment either posts or does not; after this change, one bad
anchor could lose a whole review. That is a strictly worse failure than the one it
replaces, so it is covered twice: anchors are computed from the diff's own hunk headers
rather than guessed, and on refusal `do_post` retries the same endpoint with the anchors
folded back into the body and says `[ANCHORS REFUSED -- folded into summary]`. Two tests
pin that path, including that the folded body still carries the anchored finding's text.
A review that silently sheds half its findings reads exactly like one that only had the
other half.

### Changed op tests

`None` — no `op_tests/` file is touched. The change is confined to
`.claude/skills/review-pr/`.


---

## Update — anchors point at the *section*, and what cannot be anchored gets a link

The anchoring above attaches a finding to one line. Two follow-on changes, both measured
on this bot's own archived cards.

### 1. Range anchors

**25 of 221 archived findings cite a line *range*** — `layernorm.py:1002-1012` — and every
one was anchored to line 1002 alone, so the reader saw a comment pinned to one line of a
block the finding is about, which reads as a claim about *that line*. GitHub spells a span
as `start_line` + `line` with a `start_side`/`side` for each end; a cited range is now
anchored as one.

Both endpoints **and every line between** must be commentable. That is exactly "inside one
hunk" — `commentable()` holds one contiguous run per hunk — and checking the two endpoints
alone would accept a span across the gap between hunks, which is a malformed range, which
fails the whole review. When only part of the span is in the diff, the end that *is* takes
a single-line anchor rather than the finding being dropped.

The span pattern is deliberately tight — ASCII hyphen, no surrounding whitespace. A loose
one reads the real card sentence `flash_kda.py:381 — 6 published tuning candidates` as the
backwards span `381..6`. Over 221 findings the tight form matched 25 spans and no false
positive; the loose form added that one sentence and nothing true.

### 2. Permalinks for what cannot be anchored

A citation whose line the diff does not reach cannot be anchored — GitHub is right to
refuse it — and used to sit in the summary as bare `moe.py:5220` text the reader had to go
and find. It now also gets a blob permalink pinned to the **head SHA**, alone on its own
line, which is the only place GitHub expands one into the code it names. Pinned and not a
branch: a link that drifts off the code it was written about is a wrong anchor arriving
late. The finding's own `path:line` text is untouched — the link is *in addition*.

### Neither is invented

Both run through the gate anchoring already had. A citation `check_citations.py` flagged,
or a card it never ran on, gets **no anchor and no link**. A path that does not resolve to
a file this PR touched gets no link either: a blob URL built from an unresolved basename is
a guess, and a link to the wrong code is worse than no link, for the same reason a wrong
anchor is.

### Measured

Replaying eight real cards against the diffs they were written for — 37 findings:

| | count |
|---|---|
| span anchor | 11 |
| single-line anchor | 16 |
| permalink only | 2 |
| nothing | 8 |

Auditing every span citation in the 57-card corpus: **23 of 35 span-anchor cleanly**, 1
falls back to an endpoint (part of the span is outside the diff), and 11 resolve to no file
in the diff — a vLLM path, an ambiguous basename matching two changed files, context code
the PR does not touch — and so are correctly left alone. None was too wide for `MAX_SPAN`.

Replaying also found a defect this change introduced: when a span collapses to one endpoint
the summary index stripped `path:563` and left the line opening with a bare `-569`. Fixed,
and pinned by a test.

### The all-or-nothing boundary, again

A malformed span is a **new way** to fail the whole call. The degrade-to-summary fallback
covers it like any other refusal, and a test now pins that a refused *range* review degrades
with the span finding's text intact and folded as `path:101-104`, not as a bare line.

`_publish_test.py` goes from 17 cases to 33. `check_prompts.py` gains two drift checks that
build a review over a synthetic **two-hunk** diff and assert the shape GitHub will take —
`start_line < line`, matching sides, span inside one hunk, permalinks gated — rather than
the source that produced it.

### Not verified

**Nothing here has been sent to GitHub.** Every run was dry-run or `--payload`; no code in
this PR has ever made a live review call. That the API accepts these exact payloads —
`start_line`/`start_side` as built, and the hunk-containment rule as modelled — is
unverified, and the degrade-to-summary fallback is what stands behind that uncertainty.

### 🏷️ CI Guide

**Runs automatically on every PR:**
- ✅ Pre-checks (submodule verification, code formatting)
- ✅ Aiter op tests (gfx942 + gfx950)
- ✅ Triton tests on MI35X (only when `aiter/ops/triton/**` or related paths are changed)

**Extended tests (opt-in via labels):**

| Label | Tests |
|-------|-------|
| `ci:gfx1250-ffm-triton` | Run the five-shard gfx1250 FFM Triton test suite |
| `ci:triton-300x` | Run an additional Triton test job on MI300X in PRs (added automatically when gfx942 configs change); main branch always runs both MI35X and MI300X |
| `ci:triton-355` | Run the full Triton test suite on MI35X, not only the tests the change affects |
| `ci:windows` | Windows JIT op smoke test on the gfx1201 ROCm runner |
| `ci:multi-gpu` | Aiter multi-GPU tests on the 8-GPU runner |
| `ci:sglang` | SGLang integration tests: DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 accuracy, Qwen 3.5 accuracy |
| `ci:atom` | ATOM benchmark: DeepSeek-R1-0528, GPT-OSS-120B |
| `ci:atom_full` | ATOM accuracy suite for PR and main models from ATOM `models_accuracy.json` |
| `ci:vllm` | vLLM benchmark: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MiniMax-M3-MXFP4 |
| `ci:all` | All standard extended tests (excludes `ci:atom_full`) |

> Only add `ci:atom_full` for FlyDSL or Triton upgrades.
> Add labels via the sidebar or `gh pr edit 7303 --add-label <label>`

**One backend per PR:**
A PR changes one kernel backend: `[Triton/Gluon]` (Triton and Gluon count as one), `[HIP]`, `[ASM]`, `[CK]`, `[OPUS]` or `[FlyDSL]`. If the title ends up with two backend tags, split the PR -- as [stacked pull requests](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/get-started/about-stacked-prs) when one part cannot merge without the other.

**PR title tags & labels:**
Component tags (`[Triton/Gluon]`, `[HIP]`, `[CK]`, `[ASM]`, ...) are added to the PR title and as PR labels automatically from the changed files and re-synced on every push — change-type tags like `[fix]`/`[Perf]`, op tags like `[MLA]`, and human labels (`ci:*`) are left untouched. Add the `no-auto-title` label to stop the title rewrites; labels stay in sync either way.

# NOT READY FOR HUMAN REVIEW

## PR Self-Review

Revision `33746f0df707` · mode `shadow`

**Waiting for the PR author.** The readiness report will appear after the self-review answers are complete for this revision.

### Questions to answer in the PR description

1. What behavior does this PR change, and why is the existing behavior insufficient?
2. What did you validate, and what remains unverified? Include commands, hardware/configuration and results.
3. What is the most important boundary or failure mode introduced by this change, and what evidence covers it?
4. For every changed `op_tests/` file, what behavior does it cover and why is it not redundant? Write `None` if no op test changed.

Edit the `PR Self-Review` section in the PR description. Include the current revision SHA; this comment refreshes automatically.

### Missing or invalid answers
- FAIL — `Reviewed revision` must contain at least the first 7 characters of the current head SHA

<sub>Shadow mode reports what would block but keeps the status successful. Set `AITER_PR_SELF_REVIEW_MODE=enforce` only after reviewing real false positives.</sub>
